lvuyk4:149: In the requirement self-iteration case, QA's right to reject is a key emergent node. In practice, you should consciously design which roles can say "no" to other roles' outputs and under what conditions: what are the entry standards? How is the correction loop triggered after rejection? This mechanism is not defined once and finished; it iterates continuously across multiple rounds of collaboration. It is recommended that each role have at least two explicit "rejection trigger conditions", with a correction path defined for each condition.
m5bumi:210: Most AI Agent implementations remain at the "tool enhancement" level: Agents are plugged into existing processes and become more efficient, but the way the organization operates does not change. Agent Room differs by placing multiple roles in the same contextual field—product, QA, architecture, full-stack—allowing them to correct each other and make joint judgments within the same information. This requires the organization to not only support multi-Agent collaboration at the technical level, but also to systematically design role definitions, information-sharing protocols, and decision-transfer mechanisms. Tools can be replicated at zero cost, but context integration across roles requires sustained organizational investment.
nt9da:197: The core hypothesis of Agent Room is that "if multiple roles are placed in the same contextual field, they will judge for themselves whether to intervene." But context sharing itself does not automatically produce collaboration—it requires mechanism design: when a role intervenes (entry threshold), when to stay silent (avoid interference), and when to push forward (closed loop completion). In Example 2, the technical support Agent did not stop at the superficial conclusion of "logs are normal", but continued to dig deeper, reflecting the combination of shared context and proactive judgment. Without such a proactive intervention mechanism, context is only read-only material and will not generate collaborative behavior.
o583bn:210: In a traditional single-Agent process, QA is a post-hoc verifier—development finishes, QA tests, and multiple Agents execute in sequence but lack lateral correction. In Agent Room, QA intervenes early, proactively sets release preconditions, and rejects acceptance when the entry criteria are not met. This is the first observable sign of multi-Agent collaborative emergence: one role begins to exercise veto power over another role's output. This is not pre-written into a process node, but rather QA judges on its own in the shared context that "the current completed facts are insufficient to enter testing" and then @s development to supply evidence. This lateral constraint mechanism is core evidence of emergence.

r6ekta:229: The essence of the three-layer evolution is a leap from automated tools to collaborative judgment entities. In the first stage, Aone Agent turned R&D processes into pages, with AI as an enhanced executor—processes are defined by humans, and AI just runs faster. In the second stage, OpenClaw achieved full-chain automation: Agents can read requirements, identify repositories, and infer technology stacks on their own. But neither stage broke beyond the "tool" category. The essential leap of the third stage is that the system begins to grow a "brain" and can make decision judgments, rather than merely executing preset paths. The key to this leap is not how many tools or CLIs are integrated, but whether multiple roles can form a true judgment closed loop in the same context.
